headline: ERS experts take part in 11th European Conference on Tobacco Control in Istanbul
dek: The European Respiratory Society said its experts played a central role at the ENSP-ECTC, held amid rising youth e-cigarette use in the WHO European Region.
body:
The European Respiratory Society (ERS) said its experts played a central role at the 11th European Conference on Tobacco Control (ENSP-ECTC), held in Istanbul earlier this month. In a LinkedIn post, the society said the event brought together academics, health professionals, policymakers and civil society representatives.

The ERS said the conference took place against the backdrop of continued growth in e-cigarette use among young people in Europe. It cited a figure of as many as 14.3% of 13–15-year-olds in the WHO European Region using e-cigarettes, which it described as the highest rate of any WHO region.

According to the ERS, the event aimed to ensure that child protection is placed at the centre of EU law during the revision of the EU Tobacco Products and Tobacco Advertising Directives. The society linked to a longer online account of the conference.

The post also referenced the ENSP, the European Network for Smoking and Tobacco Prevention, in connection with the conference.
key_quote: ERS experts played a central role as academics, health professionals, policymakers and civil society representatives met in Istanbul earlier this month
